notes: kb/Work PB5123 LANDED: the refusal half is closed. §1985:VI.6.3.3 GRL2.2: when the word after NOT is not GREATER, >, LESS, <, EQUAL or =, 'The NOT is interpreted as a logical operator and, therefore, the implied insertion of subject or relational operator results in a negated relation condition'. succeedingCondition now carries a third alternative, negatedAbbreviatedRelation (NOT abbreviatedRelation), whose left-edge predicate logicalNotBeforeRelationalOperator is GRL2.1 (the six words, and NOT, which no reading lets follow NOT), so it never competes with the comparisonOperator alternatives that open on NOT; ConditionBinder.BindCondition binds it as BoundNot over BindAbbreviatedRelation, so the stated operator is the one carried on. A > B AND NOT >= C OR D is ((A > B) AND (NOT (A >= C))) OR (A >= D), and NOT <= and NOT IS > read the same way; the witness pb5123_logical_not_before_relop runs the five table examples' kinds and T8-T13 (each fails if the form is refused or the negated operator is carried). ISO 2002 prohibited the form (§2002:F.1 item 22), so VersionConformancePass.VisitNegatedAbbreviatedRelation refuses it from 2002 with COBOL0902 (construct abbreviated-not-logical-removed-2002; a warning under --permissive, the 85 meaning kept), witnessed by cases/8.7.5-Relational-operators/pb1034-abbreviated-not-gteq (refused at 2002, 2014 and 2023 with COBOL0902; it was COBOL0001 at every edition, 85 included). Still refused at 85, correctly: AND NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO C (rule (1) makes NOT part of an operator 1985 does not have) and AND NOT NOT > C. The row's earlier reading: succeedingCondition offered abbreviatedRelation (NOT < etc. inside comparisonOperator) or unaryLogicalExpression (NOT + bare object), and BindFlatSequence/AbbrevCarry insert the carried subject and operator; probes at --std 85 (work-rd-04/c3/a2.cob) of A = B OR C OR NOT D, A > B AND IS NOT < C, NOT A > B OR > C AND D, A < B OR NOT C AND >= D and A > B AND C = D OR 9 all expand as the text says.

next.reason: 1985: otherwise 'The NOT is interpreted as a logical operator and, therefore, the implied insertion of subject or relational operator results in a negated relation condition', under the format '[NOT] [relational-operator] object' (§1985:VI.6.3.3), so a logical NOT may precede a stated operator that does not begin with the six words, e.g. 'a > b AND NOT >= c' (>= is a 1985 operator, §1985:VI.6.3.1.1 'IS NOT LESS THAN is equivalent to IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO') meaning NOT (a >= c). 2023 keeps logical NOT before a bare object with the same five expansions (§2023:8.8.4.12.4 GR1), but the format makes NOT an alternative to the relational operator, not a prefix to it (§2023:8.8.4.12.2, rendered page 233), and the note states 'However, NOT cannot immediately precede an extended-relational operator'. A valid 1985 abbreviation with a logical NOT followed by a stated operator is refused in 2023.
